text:
maya: Heads up — SCIM heartbeats to our vendor IdP started failing right after the KMS signing key rotation at ~10:02UTC. Users are stuck in pending provisioning. Logs show token verification errors.

devin: Can you paste the error? Also which alias was rotated?

maya: log snippet:
```
SCIM/heartbeat: request rejected, status=401, reason=invalid_signature, detail=signature verification failed for kid=prod-idp-signing-v2
stack: oidc.jwt.verify -> jwkset.fetch -> key not found
```
We rotated alias `alias/prod-idp-signing` -> `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:xxxx:key/abcd-v2` about 8m ago (deploy-bot announced it).

idp-bot: automated: KMS alias update completed by infra-deploy-bot at 2026-03-20T10:02:15Z. JWKS cached at vendor side may take up to 5 minutes to refresh.

sam: That sounds like the vendor still validates against old key material. Two possible causes: 1) our signing kid changed but JWKS hasn't propagated; 2) the token issuer now uses a different kid and vendor IDP can't fetch new jwks due to caching or network egress rules.

devin: Quick triage steps I ran: introspect the last SCIM JWT locally -> failed. Curl token introspection against our introspection endpoint: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/introspect \
  -H 'Authorization: Basic <client>' \
  -d 'token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InByb2QtdWlkIn0...' | jq .
```
Response: {"active": false, "error": "invalid_signature"}  — kid in token = prod-idp-signing-v2 but our JWKS endpoint currently serves kid prod-idp-signing (v1).

nicole: Could this be the KMS alias pointing to a new key with a new public component but we forgot to update the published JWKS or proxy that signs tokens for SCIM?

maya: Exactly. Sequence of events: rotate KMS key -> infra updated alias -> token signer started using new key (new kid) -> we failed to publish matching JWKS or the vendor cached the old one. Vendor rejects token, SCIM heartbeats fail, provisioning stalls.

ops-oncall: Mitigation options: 1) revert alias to previous key (fast but requires KMS access & audit ticket), 2) publish both JWKS entries temporarily (v1 and v2) so vendor can validate, 3) ask vendor to refresh JWKS (slower). Which do we want?

auditor: Note that reverting alias will create audit log entries; we need a short blameless note in the ticket. Also confirm we keep the previous key material available for cross-check if required by compliance.

devin: I spun up a quick proxy to serve a JWKS that contains both keys and updated the token signer to include both kids in headers. Patch applied to canary (token-signer-canary) — testing now.

maya: After proxy patch, heartbeats returned to 200 within 90s. Vendor acknowledged and accepted tokens again. SCIM sync resumed; pending users started provisioning.

sam: Follow-ups: - Add rolling key rotation playbook (include JWKS publish + vendor refresh step) - Add an integration test that validates vendor can verify tokens post-rotation using a short-lived test token - Add alert: SCIM provisioning pending > 5m triggers idp-integration pager.

devin: I'll open a postmortem doc and include the exact KMS commands used, timeline, and CISO review notes. Also propose we expand our deployment job to update JWKS entry and hit vendor refresh endpoint as part of rotation.

nicole: Can we also add RBAC check: ensure only infra-deploy-bot has permission to UpdateAlias and require a second approver for production alias changes?

auditor: +1. Put the change through change advisory board (CAB) and capture KMS rotation runbook in compliance artifacts.

maya: Thanks all. Creating incident ticket now: INC-2026-3181. Will attach logs, the revert/patch commands, and remediation checklist. :white_check_mark:
